question: An engineering team already has a working internal Slack bot with OAuth handled by Anthropic's published Slack MCP server. They now want Claude Code to post release notes to a channel. What should they do instead of writing a custom tool from scratch?
options: A) Use the built-in Bash tool to call curl against the Slack API endpoints from the shell
B) Create a Skill that contains hard-coded Slack API request examples to copy manually
C) Connect the existing Slack MCP server so Claude reuses its messaging tools and authentication
D) Write a custom tool whose handler re-implements the Slack Web API client and OAuth refresh flow
correct_answers: C) Connect the existing Slack MCP server so Claude reuses its messaging tools and authentication
explanations: Shelling out with curl bypasses structured tool schemas and error handling, and requires managing credentials manually inside the Bash environment.
A Skill can describe how to use a tool, but it cannot itself authenticate or make network calls, so release notes would never actually reach Slack.
Correct: when a maintained MCP server already exists for a service, connecting to it reuses its authentication and tool definitions instead of duplicating that work in a custom tool.
Reimplementing the OAuth flow and API client duplicates work the existing MCP server already solved, adding maintenance burden without adding capability.
